page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a Cloud GPU server instance featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel CPU with 8 shared vCPUs, structured as 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor runs at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and is supported by 40.0 GB of system memory, yielding 5.0 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, the instance includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with a 0.3333 allocation, providing 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is delivered via a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average-tier performance across standard CPU, memory, and database operations. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1786.68 and a multi-core score of 14175.12. PassMark CPU performance is recorded at 14090.9, while PassMark database operations reached 3658.8. Large block memory bandwidth is measured at 88.57 GB/sec for read operations and 52.63 GB/sec for write operations. In contrast to these average-tier baseline metrics, the instance demonstrates top-tier performance in large language model inference benchmarks, processing prompts at 3147.67 tokens/sec and generating text at 107.73 tokens/sec using a medium 7B model.

The combination of a shared CPU allocation and a fractional GPU presents a resource density tradeoff. This architecture serves as a qualitatively cost-efficient entry point for workloads that require GPU acceleration and NVMe storage but do not demand a full, dedicated GPU card. This server profile is suited for small to medium LLM inference, machine learning model prototyping, database operations, and general-purpose applications requiring moderate parallel processing capabilities.
